document.title: Instruction to Nominate Four Terrorist Leaders for Listing by the UN 1267 Sanctions Committee (State 070339)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), The Haqqani History: Bin Ladin's Advocate Inside the Taliban
document.note: [Unclassified] The page gives no separate summary. Documents 6 and 7 together show that Haqqani leaders were already on the UN 1267 Committee list of individuals associated with bin Laden, the Taliban or al-Qaida, and subject to a travel ban, arms embargo and asset freeze. Those named include Jalaluddin, his sons Badruddin, Nasiruddin and Sirajuddin, and his brother Khalil Haqqani.

key_claims: Nasiruddin Haqqani raised funds for the Haqqani Network in the Gulf and UAE from 2005 to 2009.
The Haqqani Network's funding came from Gulf donations, drug trafficking and al-Qa'ida payments as of mid-2007.
The Haqqani Network is led by Jalaluddin Haqqani's three oldest sons and operates from North Waziristan.
Gul Agha Ishakzai served as Mullah Omar's financial secretary and gatekeeper.
Amir Abdullah hosted Taliban leadership meetings at his Karachi guesthouse and helped Taliban members settle in Pakistan in 2001.
